1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.title: Carrick understands jeers from Man Utd fans after Mainoo substitution
1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.subtitle: Manchester United's travelling fans made their feelings known when Kobbie Mainoo was substituted with 10 minutes to play against Fulham.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick understands the "emotional" reactions to Manchester United's recent struggles, after his decision to withdraw Kobbie Mainoo against Fulham was booed by their travelling fans.
With just five points on the board after five games, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign, having also taken five at this stage of 2014-15.

Things could have been worse for the Red Devils at Craven Cottage on Sunday, too, as Matheus Cunha's deflected strike snatched a point in the 89th minute, after Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal had put them on the back foot.
With United 1-0 down and chasing the game, Carrick's choice to replace Mainoo with Mason Mount in the 80th minute was loudly jeered by the away end.
Mainoo had completed 64 of his 68 passes, 27 of which were in the final third, with only Bryan Mbeumo (100%) and Harry Maguire (95.8%) bettering his 94.1% pass accuracy among United's starters.
But Carrick feels that reaction came from a place of frustration and understands the disgruntled feeling among the fanbase.
"There are always going to be certain reactions when you're making changes," Carrick said. "I've spoken to Kobbie after the game and he's absolutely fine.
"I understand at times when we are chasing the game, everyone's a little bit emotional. The supporters are – as they should be – desperate for us to do the right thing.
"But I don't take any negatives or offence to it. I think we've just got to try and keep doing the right things to get back into the game.
"The supporters were unbelievable, I have to say, all the way through. They stuck with the boys and supported them.
"At least we've given them something small at the end to take from it, and I'm sure there's more to come."

With United 12th in the Premier League table going into the extended international break, the Opta supercomputer only assigns them a 17% chance of qualifying for the Champions League, but Carrick is sure there are plenty of twists and turns ahead.
"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick said. "It's a long season, and you're going to have these spells through a season. That's part of the journey. It's not a sprint; it's a long effort.
"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points, so I'm not saying everything's great. I understand the frustration. We wanted to be better, and we wanted to do other things.
"But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club and within the group. The players didn't have that on the pitch, and that's what will carry us through the season, without a doubt."
United face Tottenham, who are still winless and prop up the table, in their next Premier League game on October 10.

1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.title: Amorim vows not to repeat Man Utd errors with Milan
1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.subtitle: AC Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A under Ruben Amorim rolled on, and he intends to continue allowing his team to play with freedom.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim insists he will not be pushed into making the same tactical mistakes he made during his stint with Manchester United, now he is in charge of AC Milan.
Amorim's unbeaten start in Serie A continued on Sunday with a comfortable 3-0 win against Lecce at San Siro, with the result moving Milan up to fifth in the standings.
Christian Pulisic's sensational touch and finish put Milan ahead early on, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira sealed the win for the Rossoneri during a dominant second half.
Milan's victory saw them remain unbeaten in their opening five Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23 (W3 D2).

Amorim (W3 D2) has become only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to not taste defeat in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.

Speaking after the game, Amorim revealed he allowed his side to play with "freedom", and when asked about the reasoning behind that decision, he highlighted his turbulent tenure at Old Trafford, where he was reluctant to adapt his style of play.
"It's an observation of the games and the characteristics," Amorim told DAZN, as quoted by Football Italia.

"Of course, I listen to the players, but a manager, especially in a big team, is always listening to the players, seeing and understanding them, but every player wants to push the game towards their characteristics, and if you want to have an identity, that is hard.
"It's always my decision. What I felt in the last games is the same that I felt at Manchester United, and I cannot make the same mistake.
"Sometimes we don't have the perfect characteristics to play in that way, and if we don't have them, we have to adapt. I think today worked.
"In another game, we can return to the build-up with three [at the back]. The important thing is to have different ways of playing.

"That's especially important in Italy, because the managers are really smart, they mark really well one against one, and when they lose the reference to what we want to do, it's harder for them to understand their mobility, just as they make it harder for me to understand their teams."

Milan have now won their first two home Serie A matches of a season while keeping a clean sheet in both for the first time since 2020-21, when they beat Bologna 2-0 and Spezia 3-0 under Stefano Pioli.

Their dominance was backed up by the underlying metrics, too. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.93 from their 10 attempts, while also restricting Lecce to a measly xG total of 0.17 from six shots.
It was a much-needed victory heading into the international break, with Milan coming into the clash with Lecce without a win in three matches in all competitions (D2 L1).
Roma, Inter and Lazio are the early pace setters in the division, all sitting two points clear of Milan, and Amorim feels his team are on the right track.
"If you look at the way we play, Roma and Inter had more time as a team, you can see the patterns are there," Amorim added.
"We didn't lose so many points, we dropped two to Lazio and Juventus away, so not everything is bad.

"Sometimes it looks like that, especially after recent results, but we have to see the balance. We won today against a good team that is doing well, but it is a different team, and sometimes we will have issues.
"It's a process, I think we should have more points, as against Juventus we weren't playing so well, but we were 30 seconds off getting three points.
"Even against Lazio, if you look at the balance of the game, I feel we deserved a little bit more."

1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.title: Colwill expects Chelsea to be better after international break
1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.subtitle: Chelsea's strong start to the season fizzled out before the international break, but Levi Colwill is confident they can improve after it.
paragraphs: Levi Colwill has backed Chelsea to come out on the other side of the international break "flying".
Chelsea made a strong start to life under Xabi Alonso, winning four of their first five matches across all competitions (L1).

However, having had to come from behind to draw 2-2 with high-flying Hull City, the Blues were then thrashed 3-0 by Brentford in their final match before the extended international break to leave them winless in three league games.
Chelsea have already lost more Premier League matches in 2026 (11) than they did in the entirety of 2025 (10).

Alonso became only the sixth Premier League boss to see his side concede at least two goals in each of his first five games, after Mick McCarthy, Sammy Lee, Terry Connor, Slavisa Jokanovic, and Scott Parker.

And Chelsea's defensive woes have been highlighted on multiple occasions, even before Alonso's appointment; since the start of last season, they have conceded 23 Premier League goals from non-penalty set-pieces, now the joint-most of any side, along with Bournemouth.
Colwill admitted the start of the season was not what Chelsea expected, but he wants to use the extended international break to get back on track.
"[There have been] some good bits, some other not so good bits," he said, as quoted by Chelsea's website.
"Luckily, we've got a while now to try and improve.
"Hopefully, we will come out the other side flying, pick up our play, and become a better team."
Chelsea return to action at home to Bournemouth on October 10.

1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.title: Xavi promises 'intensity and passion' in new-look Netherlands approach
1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.subtitle: Xavi will take charge of the Netherlands for the first time this international break, and he is preparing his team for a new approach.
paragraphs: Xavi has promised to bring "intensity, passion and a good rhythm" to the Netherlands' play as he prepares to take charge for the first time.
The Spaniard was named as the Oranje's head coach on a four-year deal after Ronald Koeman left in the wake of a disappointing World Cup campaign over the summer.
While the Netherlands enjoyed an unbeaten group stage, they fell at the first hurdle in the knockouts, losing on penalties to Morocco.
Xavi, a former World Cup winner with Spain, will face Germany in his first game in charge in Amsterdam on Thursday, as the Netherlands kick off their Nations League campaign.

Koeman was criticised at times for taking a defensive approach with his tactics, and while Xavi did not give away too many hints about his approach, he outlined what he expects from his players on Monday.
"Everything is new ​for me and for the staff, so it will first be to get to know each other, ​know all the players, insist or convince them about our way to play," Xavi told reporters.
"We don't have too much time. But no excuses; every coach is in the same situation.

"I want to explain the values that ​we want from the squad. I want to show them that I'm open to them; I want ​to help them. I want to enjoy the process with them. We want to create a family; we want ‌to ⁠create a big group.
"The players must come to the national team with happiness, but at the end, the main goal is to win.

"You cannot promise results, but ​we will work ⁠for results. I can promise that we will play with intensity, with passion, with a good rhythm, trying to be competitive and trying to ​take the initiative in the game. This is for sure.
"There's going ​to be ⁠a different way of playing. I don't want to compare, and I don't want to talk about the past. I respect Ronald a lot. But I'm focused on the present."
Virgil van Dijk will remain the Netherlands' captain, having revealed on Sunday that he plans to keep representing his national team until Euro 2028.
"It ​was a really good meeting," Xavi said of meeting Van Dijk in Liverpool to discuss his Netherlands future.
"He was very honest. He has the capacity to continue. He's a good leader. He's positive, ​he's motivated. He's ready to be the leader."

1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.title: Palmer and Rice withdraw from England squad as Gibbs-White, Garner come in
1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.subtitle: Thomas Tuchel will be without Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Marcus Rashford for England's upcoming Nations League fixtures.
paragraphs: Cole Palmer and Declan Rice are part of a quintet of players who have withdrawn from England duty.
Palmer, who missed out on England's World Cup squad, was selected by Thomas Tuchel for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League matches.
He has already registered four Premier League goal involvements this season (two goals, two assists).
However, the Chelsea playmaker has now opted out of the squad as he nurses an injury.
It is the same case for Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo.
Tuchel has called up Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner as replacements.
No player has scored more Premier League goals in 2026 than Nottingham Forest attacker Gibbs-White (13, level with Erling Haaland).

Garner, meanwhile, made his England debut during the March international window, and impressed against Uruguay and Japan, but the Everton midfielder ultimately missed out on a call-up for the World Cup.
The pair will now get a chance to impress in fixtures against world champions Spain, with a double-header against Czechia following, either side of a clash with Croatia.

1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.title: Luis Enrique not taking Classique triumph for granted
1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.subtitle: Marquinhos struck the winner as Paris Saint-Germain overcame Marseille in Sunday's matchup between France's two most successful clubs.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain can never take a win over Classique rivals Marseille for granted, after they battled to a 2-1 success at the Stade Velodrome.
Marquinhos' 74th-minute strike settled the contest as PSG claimed back-to-back Ligue 1 victories, having started their campaign with three winless games.
The Brazilian's goal came just two minutes after Angel Gomes got Marseille back on level terms, with that strike also coming hot on the heels of Ferran Torres' opener.
Marseille had captain Timothy Weah sent off shortly after going 2-1 down, with the United States international hauling Nuno Mendes down from behind while already on a yellow card.

PSG have now won 10 of their last 14 away Ligue 1 games against Marseille (D3 D1), though Nayef Aguerd missed a huge chance to snatch a point for OM deep into stoppage time, as he headed wide on the stretch.
And Luis Enrique says three points will never come easily for any visiting side at the Velodrome.
"It was the match we had planned for, with a lot of difficulties. Everyone said it would be easy, but playing at the Velodrome is not an easy thing," he told Ligue 1+.
"We tried to play, we created fewer chances in the first half because the opponent defended very well. In the second half, everything changed, we made a very good effort."

The result piles more pressure on Bruno Genesio, who is the first Marseille boss to lose four of his first five league games in charge of the club since the duo of Willy Kohut and Andre Gascard in 1938.

Marseille will spend the three-week international break 17th in the Ligue 1 table, with this the latest point into a season that they have sat in the relegation zone since 2011-12, when they were 20th with three points after six games and ultimately finished 10th.
But Luis Enrique expects them to come good eventually, saying: "Nothing was easy, we saw a very good OM team, with the way they defended. They have a great coach, I'm sure they will improve."
Genesio himself, however, admits Marseille's results have fallen well short of the required standard and has revealed he will hold talks with the club's hierarchy during the break.
"It's funny, everyone wishes me good luck. I'm a coach, so obviously I'm linked to the performances and results, especially at a club like OM," he said.
"This is insufficient, I assume my share of responsibility, as others will have to assume it too.
"I'm not there yet, I'm going to digest this defeat, talk to my staff, talk to my directors.
"Because I think – and I'm trying to weigh my words – that it's not normal for OM to be in this situation."
While PSG host Le Mans in their next Ligue 1 game on October 10, Marseille go to Troyes the following day.

1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.title: Spalletti relieved to see Juventus banish Sassuolo 'doubts' against Atalanta
1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.subtitle: Having seen their unbeaten Serie A start halted by Sassuolo on matchday four, Juventus bounced back with an impressive win over Atalanta.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti admitted Juventus' defeat to Sassuolo last week had created doubt in the Bianconeri's ranks, and he was delighted to see them banish that feeling by beating Atalanta.
Juve suffered their first defeat of the Serie A campaign on matchday four, conceding a stoppage-time winner to Vasilije Adzic in a 3-2 loss to Sassuolo.
However, they bounced back in style on Sunday with a 2-0 success against Atalanta and their former head coach Maurizio Sarri, with Francisco Conceicao and Bremer on target.

          Five Knee-Jerk Reactions to Premier League 2026-27 Matchday 5
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re back with our weekly dose of knee-jerk reactions to the weekend’s Premier League action.
Every week here on Opta Analyst, we do something we don’t normally do and come to a load of conclusions based on just a single round of Premier League matches.
We usually rely on large data sets to make our judgements, but in this weekly column we react quickly and maybe a little too hastily.
It’s all a bit of fun, and many of our five reactions for this week will swiftly prove to be nothing more than exactly what we called them: knee-jerk.
But some might just hold up in the weeks to come. Read on to see which way you think these week’s conclusions will eventually go.

Coming into Matchday 5, it felt like there was no stopping Arsenal. They’d won all four Premier League games, as well as three more in other competitions, and few of their opponents had caused them any real problems at all.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side had produced some impressive results early in the season, but nobody expected them to blow Arsenal away quite like they did on Saturday.

They pressed the champions with a vicious and suffocating relentlessness that meant Arsenal just could not get any kind of grip on the game. Brighton forced a colossal 15 high turnovers (winning possession within 40 metres of the opposition's goal line), which is the second most by any team in the Premier League this season, behind only Brighton against an Aston Villa side who played most of that game with just 10 men (19).

They also recognised how difficult it is to carve out clear-cut chances against this Arsenal side, so shot on sight, often from distance. They scored twice from range to take Arsenal’s total to a league-high three goals conceded from outside the box this season.

Was this the blueprint for how to take the champions down, or a mere – and very natural – day off for the best team in the world right now? We’ll see if anyone else can do this to them after they’ve gathered their thoughts during the international break.
Some say you make your own luck, but there’s no denying that Spurs have been incredibly fortunate not to be relegated in the last two utterly dismal seasons.

In 2024-25, they were entirely reliant on the dreadful form of the promoted sides, who were so bad that there was never really a relegation battle of any sort. Then, last season, they escaped by the skin of their teeth after failing to address their myriad of problems in either transfer window.

Now, five games into 2026-27 and after a summer of upheaval, they are bottom of the table and staring at the very real possibility of another flirtation with the drop despite spending more than £300 million.

They have a lot of talent in their squad now, and certainly appear to have more potential, particularly in attack, than they did last term. Against Aston Villa on Saturday, they created more than enough, notably when the game was still level, to take control of the game, but failed to take their chances and were punished in brutal fashion. They won on xG but remain winless in actuality, with just two points from five games and a goal difference of -6.
It is now their worst ever start to a Premier League season and has left them with a lot of improving to do to avoid the possibility of another 17th-place finish – or worse.

We’ve learned over the last two years that nothing can be taken for granted with this club, and with no other team looking anything like as hopeless so far this season, there is every chance they get themselves into yet more trouble.
Brian Brobbey isn’t the most fashionable of footballers, and his physical approach to the game may mean he never gets the chance to play for a big-six club.

But even if he doesn’t play for a Champions League club that never lifts the ball off the floor and always has more than 60% possession, there is absolutely no denying what a handful he is. He deserves far more respect than many give him.

In Sunderland’s defeat to Manchester City this weekend, he scored three times from just five shots and became only the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler vs Aston Villa in November 1998, Dirk Kuyt vs Manchester United in March 2011, and Romelu Lukaku vs United in May 2013.

He was extremely unfortunate to also end up on the losing side, too, becoming the sixth player ever to score a hat-trick and lose a Premier League game, and the first since Roque Santa Cruz for Blackburn vs Wigan in December 2007.

3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.title: Spain extend De la Fuente's contract through to Euro 2032
3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.subtitle: After he led Spain to European and world titles, Luis de la Fuente's future is secured for another six years.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente will stay on as Spain's head coach through to 2032, after the Spanish Football Federation extended his contract.

De la Fuente took over in December 2022 following Luis Enrique's resignation in the wake of Spain's disappointing showing at the World Cup in Qatar, and he has enjoyed huge success in his first four years.

The 65-year-old, who spent nine years with Spain's youth teams before taking over the senior team, led them to the 2022-23 Nations League title, as well as triumphs at Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.
La Roja beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the World Cup final in July to secure their second title.
De la Fuente's current deal was due to run until the end of Euro 2028, but he will now remain in his post for an additional four years, which includes a World Cup title defence as co-hosts in 2030.
"We are seeking a project of stability and confidence," RFEF president Rafael Louzan said.
"This proposal is based on confidence in Luis de la Fuente and the sporting project he leads, for a multi-year cycle of competitions and major tournaments.
"We are talking about the most decorated coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, Luis de la Fuente deserves a long future at the RFEF."
Spain are unbeaten in their last 38 matches in all competitions, the longest-ever run by any European or South American team in history.
At this summer's World Cup, they lifted the trophy having conceded just one goal in their eight games, the fewest goals conceded by any team in a World Cup-winning campaign.
In total, De la Fuente has taken charge of 49 matches across all competitions, winning 37 of those (D10 L2). His team have scored 126 goals during that time and conceded just 35.
He will now look to reach another Nations League final – having also done so in 2024-25 before losing to Portugal on penalties.
Spain begin their new campaign away to England on September 26, with a double header against Croatia to come on either side of hosting Czechia.

480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.title: Greenwood: Man City there to win in Champions League
480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.subtitle: Manchester City return to the Women's Champions League after a season-long absence, and Alex Greenwood is eyeing a deep run.
paragraphs: Alex Greenwood says Manchester City are "going to give it absolutely everything" to try and win the Women's Champions League this season.
City were absent from last season's campaign, but they are back in the competition following their Women's Super League title success in 2025-26.
Andree Jeglertz enjoyed a stellar first season with the team, and they have started their title defence in equally fine form, having won all three of their league games so far.
But their attention now turns to the Champions League, and they will begin their campaign away to Bayern Munich on Tuesday.

City are given the fourth-highest chance of winning the Champions League by the Opta supercomputer, though their 9.1% win probability is significantly lower than outright favourites Barcelona (41.2%).
Greenwood insists City have their eyes on the trophy, though.
"To qualify was massively important; it's an expectation that we have at this football club," Greenwood told UEFA's website.
"But every competition that we play in, we're there to win.

"We know it's going to be a challenge, but it's fantastic for the club. We're going to give it absolutely everything, like we do in every other competition, take it game by game and see how far we can go."
City are facing a German side for the first time in the Champions League.

Bayern, meanwhile, have won seven of their previous 11 matches against English teams in the competition (L4), including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
On their last Champions League appearance in 2024-25, City lost their last two away games, both by a 3-0 scoreline to Barcelona and Chelsea, respectively.
"I've played in this competition enough times to know what it presents and what the challenges are," Greenwood added.
"We worked really hard to get back in this competition where I think we belong. I'm just excited to embrace the challenge.
"Champions League, Women's Super League, whatever competition we're in, we're in it with a real elite mindset to go and win, and that's been our mentality for the last 18 months."

607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.subtitle: Donyell Malen will not get the chance to extend his brilliant start to the season with the Netherlands, with injury ruling him out.
paragraphs: Donyell Malen has withdrawn from the Netherlands' squad for their upcoming Nations League matches.
Malen has been in red-hot form for Roma in Serie A so far this season, and despite playing the full 90 minutes against Inter on Saturday, he will not represent his country due to injury.
It has not been specified what Malen's issue is, but he is one of two withdrawals, with Justin Kluivert also pulling out.

Since his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances, at least twice as many as any other player in the competition in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
Across Europe's big five leagues, he has scored more than any other player (Harry Kane and Raphinha have 18).
Malen has already netted six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes per goal rate in the Italian top-flight.
Xavi Hernandez, who is taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time during this extended international break, has called up Guus Til and Mexx Meerdink as replacements.
The Netherlands face Germany in their opening Nations League match on September 24, before facing Serbia away and at home on either side of their clash with Greece.

                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re five matches into the 2026-27 Premier League season, meaning we now have more information than we did at the start of the campaign. So, how have the title predictions changed in the Opta supercomputer’s model?
It’s still very early days, but the nascent Premier League table is beginning to take shape as we head into the international break.

With five wins from five, Manchester City sit at the summit as the only team with a 100% winning record. Opta’s pre-season favourites, Arsenal, are second, three points behind, with Brighton and Brentford, who have both made hugely impressive starts, rounding out the top four.
But how have those early-season results affected the Opta supercomputer’s predictions for the title? Let’s find out.
As a reminder, Arsenal were the model’s pre-season favourites. The Opta supercomputer gave them a 40.6% chance of defending their 2025-26 title on the eve of the season.
Manchester City (19.6%) were comfortably second favourites, followed by Liverpool (9.2%) and Manchester United (6.6%).
Despite suffering a heavy defeat to Brighton at the weekend, Arsenal remain the Opta supercomputer’s favourites to lift the trophy, with a 43.7% chance of winning the title.

Manchester City (39.8%) are hot on their heels. Their perfect start, as well as Arsenal’s weekend defeat, means the title race is now definitely a two-horse contest in the supercomputer’s eyes, rather than the procession many thought it might be for Arsenal.
Together, Arsenal and Man City account for 83.4% of all the title equity in the supercomputer’s predictions.

Liverpool (5.7%) are the model’s third favourites. They are currently unbeaten under new manager Andoni Iraola, but have drawn three of their five games so far. As a result, their title hopes have fallen by 3.5 percentage points, from 9.2% before the season to 5.7% now.

Brighton, the architects of Arsenal’s downfall this weekend, have made a hugely impressive start. They are the division’s top scorers with 16 goals, boast the best goal difference at +11 and handed Arsenal their first defeat since 19 April, 155 days ago. They look like the real deal.
The Seagulls are now fourth in the Opta supercomputer’s title predictions, with a 4.2% chance of winning an improbable Premier League title.
From there, a multitude of teams are clustered around the 1% mark. Brentford have a 1.2% chance, Everton 1.1%, Chelsea 1.0%, and Manchester United are given a 0.9% chance.
Manchester City’s title chances have increased by 20.2 percentage points, more any other team across the first five matchdays.
As mentioned, City began the season as the supercomputer’s second favourites, but they have made a perfect start to life under Enzo Maresca.

Maresca is the sixth manager to win his first five Premier League games in charge of a club, after Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea (six), Pep Guardiola at Manchester City (six), Craig Shakespeare at Leicester City (five), Maurizio Sarri at Chelsea (five) and Ole Gunnar Solskjær at Manchester United (six).

Arsenal’s title chances have also increased, rising 3.0 percentage points from their pre-season figure. That might seem surprising given their defeat to Brighton, but several of the teams that started the season among the favourites have already faltered.
Chelsea and Manchester United, for example, have both made poor starts, while Liverpool have dropped points in three of their first five games.
Brighton are the only other team to rise significantly. Their chances of winning the Premier League title have more than doubled (2.0% to 4.2%) following their excellent start.
It’s been a disappointing start to the campaign for Manchester United.

          WSL Matchday 3: The Opta Numbers That Defined the Weekend
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author, Gareth Boyes / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City maintained their perfect start to the season, while Arsenal dropped points at home for the second successive match. We use Opta data to uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and biggest numbers from Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 WSL season.
There was no shortage of entertainment across the third matchday of the Women’s Super League, with goals flying in around the league, though Arsenal’s struggles continued in front of goal.

Manchester City maintained their perfect start in a six-goal thriller against Liverpool, Tottenham ran riot with seven against Crystal Palace, while London City Lionesses bounced back from defeat, firing in four goals at Charlton.

Elsewhere, Chelsea made it back-to-back wins, Everton edged past West Ham, and Brighton and Aston Villa shared the points. At the Emirates, Arsenal were frustrated at home once again as Manchester United responded from their difficult start to the season to earn a 1-1 draw.
But, as ever, the scorelines only tell part of the story.
We’ve dug into the Opta data to uncover the standout individual performances and numbers that defined Matchday 3.
We’re three games into the new WSL season and Man City are the only side still with a perfect record. But Liverpool made them work for it.
City took the lead before falling 2-1 behind, only to turn the game around and eventually claim a 4-2 victory.
It was just the second time in their WSL history that City have scored first, subsequently trailed and still gone on to win, after their 3-2 victory over Reading in the 2017 Spring Series.
Khadija Shaw continued her flying start to the campaign, becoming the first player to score in each of Manchester City’s opening three matches of a WSL season.
And Liverpool remain one of her favourite opponents.

Alongside Shaw, Lauren Hemp continues to underline her status as one of the WSL’s most devastating attacking talents – and the 26-year-old reached another significant landmark after hitting 100 goal involvements last weekend.
Only Bethany England (69), Vivianne Miedema (67), Beth Mead (60), Nikita Parris (58), Shaw (55) and Fran Kirby (54) have scored in more, while Hemp is now level with Sam Kerr.
And home continues to be a particularly happy place.
Liverpool may have left Manchester empty-handed, but there was another hugely encouraging performance from summer signing Vivien Endemann.

The Germany international is making quite the impression in her first season in England. Three appearances into her WSL career and Gareth Taylor looks like he may have uncovered a real gem for this reshaped Liverpool side.

The Reds pushed City harder than anyone has so far this season, but the league leaders still found a way to win. They have won three from three, scoring 12 goals in the process. Their perfect start rolls on.
Arsenal may have extended their unbeaten run to record-breaking territory against Manchester United, but for the second successive home game, it took late drama just to rescue a point.
After being held to a goalless draw by Crystal Palace on Matchday 2, the Gunners looked set for a first league defeat of the season before finding an equaliser deep into stoppage time.
Nonetheless, that late intervention preserved an impressive record.

The previous record holder, Köln legend Dieter Müller, took 129 Bundesliga games to score 100 goals – hitting that milestone in 1977. Harry Kane has managed the feat in just 98 appearances; he could have gone until April without registering a league goal and he’d still have broken the record.
It’s been a history-making September for the England captain, whose winner against Elversberg took him to 150 goals in all competitions for Bayern – in only 153 appearances.

The 33-year-old has picked up where he left off last season, when he enjoyed a career-best 61-goal campaign, finishing as Bundesliga top scorer for the third time in as many years since joining Bayern from Tottenham.

We already knew Kane was one of the best strikers in the world, if not the best – but what we’re seeing now is that he might actually still be getting better, an astonishing possibility for a player who, based on your typical centre-forwards, should be some years past his peak (of course, Kane isn’t your typical centre-forward).

Speaking after his latest landmark achievement, Kane – who amassed 213 goals in 317 Premier League outings for Spurs, placing him behind only Alan Shearer in the competition’s all-time scoring charts – said: “I’m very proud, to be honest, to reach 100 goals in the Bundesliga. Obviously, I’ve done it in the Premier League, so now to have it in a different league is something I’m really proud of. All I can say is a big thanks to the team.”
Kane’s 101 Bundesliga goals have come at a truly prolific average of 1.03 per game. He’s already averaging 0.75 goals per game in the league this season and 0.85 in all competitions.

And none of this should come as any kind of surprise: his overall goals-per-game average for Bayern is 0.98. Were he to score a hat-trick in his side’s first match after the international break, away to local rivals Augsburg, he would pull himself to exactly a goal a game.

It’s little wonder Kane, who has found the net 44 times for club and country this calendar year, is considered one of the frontrunners to win the Ballon d’Or – an individual accolade he’s yet to claim in a career full of them. Oh, and he’s done it at exactly a goal a game.
More goalscoring milestones feel like an inevitability for Kane, who has reportedly been in talks over extending his stay at Bayern, where his current deal expires next summer.

He’s one of 56 players with 100 or more Bundesliga goals to their name – but one of only eight non-Germans. Barring a lengthy injury lay-off or unfathomable loss of form, he’ll almost certainly pass 106-goal Ailton (Brazil) and Stéphane Chapuisat (Switzerland) this term in the ranking of leading foreign Bundesliga scorers – and probably 127-goal Vedad Ibišević (Bosnia and Herzegovina) as well.

Kane can also keep working his way up Bayern’s list of top Bundesliga goalscorers – on which he currently ranks sixth. Next in his sights is Dieter Hoeneß (102 goals), followed by fellow 1980s star Roland Wohlfarth (119).

Another couple of par scoring seasons by his standards and Kane will catch two more Bayern icons: Thomas Müller (150 goals) and two-time Ballon d’Or winner Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (162). Only the top two goalscorers in Bundesliga history are – unless he keeps playing for Bayern and producing these levels into his 40s – out of his reach: Robert Lewandowski (312) and perhaps the greatest No. 9 of all time, Gerd Müller (365).

It’s also not out of the question that Kane will become Bayern’s second-highest Champions League scorer ever. He currently sits second with 34 goals, nine ahead of Arjen Robben and 23 behind Thomas Müller – and with his goals-per-game average for the club in that competition an expectedly high 0.87 as things stand, he could well surpass Müller by the end of next season if Bayern go even reasonably deep into the knockout stage.
And if contract talks progress as both parties will hope, Kane is bound to keep tearing up the division for a number of years yet.

Some unruly classes exchanged goals freely, with five different teams scoring three or more across a flurry of chaotic affairs. Others simply waited for the bell to ring, something almost impressive in the way they managed to expend so much time, energy and sweat without achieving anything noteworthy.

ftbpro_01m2zcav5cvx.title: Raphinha and the Ballon d’Or: Why the World’s Most In-Form Player Is Not Nominated
ftbpro_01m2zcav5cvx.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By James Cormack8:30 AM EDTSnubbed. / Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesPlayers have started to evolve into politicians in award season, with the leading contenders for the Ballon d’Or unabashedly campaigning in a bid to sway voters.

While Harry Kane has offered insight into his brilliance and Paris Saint-Germain’s superstars have waxed lyrical about one another, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé have been more forthright in their respective quests to claim the prestigious individual honor for the first time.

It all looks a little bit desperate, and those who like to yell at clouds would suggest that the election-like push for the award is merely further evidence of the sport‘s decline. Bayern Munich’s director of sport, Max Eberl, was right when he said: "The best players don't need to run a campaign."

One man who absolutely would’ve joined Yamal and Mbappé in campaigning fiercely is Yamal’s Barcelona teammate, Raphinha. The Brazilian believed his fifth-place finish in last year’s Ballon d’Or was unjust, and while the prolific forward is far from an on-pitch egoist, he evidently dreams of garnering the prestige that comes with claiming the prize captured by the likes of Ronaldinho, Ronaldo and Kaká.

And Raphinha is currently performing like a Ballon d’Or winner. A hat trick at Sevilla on Saturday means Barça have enjoyed their best-ever start to a La Liga season, with the Brazilian scoring 12 times in seven outings.

Curiously, though, the 29-year-old was omitted from the 30-man shortlist for this year’s award. His form at the start of the season is making a mockery of that decision, but was Raphinha’s 2025–26 season worthy of such acclaim?

Injuries curtailed the Brazilian’s 2025–26 campaign. / Maria Gracia Jimenez/Soccrates/Getty ImagesIt must be pointed out that Raphinha’s most recent antics are irrelevant in the context of the 2026 Ballon d’Or. The Brazilian is pushing to win the award next year.
For the award that’ll be handed out in October, voters are essentially taking into account the 2025–26 domestic season, as well as the World Cup.

Raphinha entered Hansi Flick’s second season off the back of a staggering 2024–25 campaign, which returned 60 goal contributions in 57 games across all competitions for Barcelona. Hence why he backed himself for last year’s award.

However, his output dipped to 29 goal contributions in 33 games, as Raphinha suffered from hamstring issues. He missed 24 games for club and country as a result, which meant he was either half-fit or unavailable in crunch time.

The 29-year-old played just 29 minutes in El Clásico and missed Barça’s Champions League quarterfinal against Atlético Madrid. Raphinha’s absence was costly, too, as Atléti held on to win 3–2 over two legs. The Brazilian had recorded six goal contributions in seven Champions League outings, paling in comparison to the likes of Mbappé (16), Kane (17) and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (16).

While Raphinha was productive when available and still a big part of a title-winning team, his hamstring woes prevented him from starring at critical junctures. He was outshone on the continental stage, and his 13 La Liga goals were matched by Villarreal’s George Mikautadze and Atléti’s Alexander Sørloth.
Raphinha may have scored every 104 minutes in all competitions, but voters have little time for such metrics—especially in a World Cup year.

Raphinha appeared just twice at the World Cup. / ROBERTO SCHMIDT/AFP/Getty ImagesThe 2026 World Cup was always going to have a major say in deciding the Ballon d’Or. It’s soccer’s grandest stage, and the tournament was dominated by superstars.

Lionel Messi’s fairytale concluded at the final hurdle, Mbappé retained the Golden Boot, while Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham (in tandem with Kane) spearheaded Norway and England’s respective campaigns.

The extent of the World Cup’s influence is highlighted by Julián Quiñones’ inclusion on the 30-man Ballon d’Or shortlist. The Mexican winger unknown by the vast majority did have an excellent season with Al Qadsiah, but he’s been recognized for the four goals he scored for the co-hosts.

Brazil entered the tournament hoping for a repeat of the previous World Cup held on North American soil. An unglamorous Seleção conquered the soccer world for the fourth time in 1994, and many believed it had the right man at the helm to guide it to a sixth crown.

But Brazil’s Carlo Ancelotti-led World Cup was a major disappointment. The five-time winners suffered its earliest exit at the tournament since 1990 by losing to Norway in the last-16, having topped a tricky Group C and scraping past Japan in the round of 32.

Much was made of Neymar Jr’s inclusion, a decision that would haunt Ancelotti, but few expected the  34-year-old to re-emerge as his country’s maverick protagonist. Instead, expectations fell on the shoulders of Vinícius Júnior and Raphinha, given their continued productivity on either side of the Clásico divide.

ftbpro_01m31f9w4ym4.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott5:30 AM EDTCole Palmer is withdrawing from the England setup. / Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty ImagesChelsea midfielder Cole Palmer is going to have to wait a little longer for his chance to prove himself to England manager Thomas Tuchel.

According to The Athletic, Palmer is due to withdraw from the England roster for this international break. “Load management” is cited as the explanation for a player who has played all but seven minutes of Chelsea’s Premier League campaign so far.

It is a tough call for Palmer, who has not played for England since March 2026 and missed this summer’s World Cup. His impressive form to start the season led to a well-earned recall, and Tuchel admitted he deserved the chance to prove he belongs on the roster full-time, but that opportunity is set to pass him by.
Those inside Chelsea will be disappointed for Palmer on a personal level but, selfishly, there will also be some understandable delight.
New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark. FREE NEWSLETTER

A summer rest worked wonders for Palmer. / Mike Hewitt/Getty ImagesThe vibe around Chelsea is a little low heading into the international break—two defeats and a draw will do that to you—but Palmer’s form has been one of the bright spots of the Xabi Alonso tenure so far.

Four goals and two assists in seven games is a strong return from a player who has openly admitted he has rediscovered his enjoyment on the pitch in Alonso’s fluid forward line. Tactics have played a big part in that, but the impact of a nice, long rest over the summer cannot be overstated.

Palmer spent the majority of last season battling the lingering impact of a groin injury which undoubtedly limited his on-field impact. He racked up just 11 goals and three assists across all competitions and could have few complaints about being left off of England’s World Cup plane.

That heartbreak brought with it an extended summer break. For the first time in months, Palmer actually had the chance to sit down. The focus between May and August was not on matches, but purely on recovery, and the results of that have been clear during the opening weeks of the season.

Chelsea fans wanted to see Palmer back in the England setup, strutting his stuff on the global stage once again, but few will complain about another three-week break for the 24-year-old if it brings the same impact as his last spell away from the pitch.
Palmer has not shown much for England under Thomas Tuchel. / Visionhaus/Getty ImagesThis is where it gets a little tricky for Palmer.

Tuchel has made no secret of his willingness to keep calling on the same core group of players—those who make a positive impact on the team both on and off the pitch—and clearly values performances for his England side over anything he watches from the stands at club level. We saw it last year with Manchester City’s Phil Foden, who was openly challenged by Tuchel for failing to turn strong performances in training into actual influence in an England shirt.

It means Tuchel’s idea of Palmer is a limited one. Since the boss’s arrival in January 2025, Palmer has played just 158 minutes for England across three appearances, with injuries and poor form both restricting his opportunities at international level. While he has been off of the scene, others have taken the opportunity to build their reputations.

Fortunately for Palmer, Tuchel has proven an openness to change. Palmer played his way into Tuchel’s thoughts this month and would likely to do again if he can keep racking up the goals and assists for Chelsea, but the bar feels like it is going to be a little bit higher for the Blues star after yet another international window away from England.

The attacking midfield spot is not one in which England is struggling. Real Madrid’s Jude Bellingham is the headline act, with a supporting cast of Eberechi Eze and Morgan Rogers in this camp. Phil Foden and Morgan Gibbs-White are waiting in the wings, as are youngsters Josh King and Max Dowman. There is a long queue for minutes and Palmer is slowly falling towards the back of it.

Given there is no major tournament in sight for England, Tuchel is likely to be flexible with his roster selections over the next 12 months. There should be more opportunities for Palmer to impress, but he can ill-afford more absences on the road to Euro 2028.

paragraphs: By Tom Gott6:30 AM EDTA tough day for Man Utd. / Tiego Grenho/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesManchester United manager Michael Carrick did his best to remain calm in the face of what Gary Neville described as “the ultimate criticism”—his team simply did not work hard enough against Fulham.

The highs of the first six months of the Carrick era have been forgotten after an ugly start to the current campaign. Only a heavily deflected 89th-minute strike from Matheus Cunha salvaged a 1–1 draw against a Fulham side still searching for their first win of the campaign, with United sitting on just one victory from their first five Premier League games.
Elimination from the Carabao Cup at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion just days earlier has seriously soured the mood, and Neville did not shy away from questioning the players.

“I’ve never seen a Man Utd team walk out of possession as much as that,” Neville reflected. “Michael has just said there was nothing wrong with the team’s energy. Michael has got to stop defending them.
“I get why he’s defending them; he’s loyal, he wants his players to work for him, and obviously there’s a long way to go in the season.
“Both teams were the same. I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen a United team walk around as much as that. No alertness, no aliveness. No ‘on your toes.’ You should always be on your toes.”
He added: “Very rarely do I say a team doesn’t work hard or is lacking in effort. That’s the ultimate criticism you can give a group of players.

“I’m always very careful to say that, but in those first 15 minutes of that second half, Man Utd and generally for the first 60 minutes, were a genuine disgrace. Nowhere near good enough without the ball.”

“The response [to Fulham’s goal] was really pleasing ... the way we went about trying to get back into the game. [We] kept the ideas, kept the patience, kept the real purpose to it. We finished on a positive, which is a small step for us ... without ­getting carried away, it’s a good step. ftbpro_01m31q0z6037.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer7:45 AM EDTMarcus Rashford did not finish the Fulham match. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesMarcus Rashford has been withdraw nfrom the England squad for the four upcoming international matches over the next 15 days, due to an ongoing hip problem—an absence that may actually facilitate improvement in the longer term.
The Manchester United forward has been out of the squad by clubmate Kobbie Mainoo, who is also thought to be carrying an injury following Sunday’s 1–1 draw against Fulham.

Rashford played 77 minutes of the contest, with United falling behind with just over an hour played and rescuing a draw with a late Matheus Cunha equalizer. Manager Michael Carrick confirmed to beIN SPORTS after: “We had to bring [Rashford] off as he had a bit of an issue.”

Carrick also said he wasn’t sure if it was a minor thing the player will quickly get over. He’d appeared to be hurt during the first half at Craven Cottage and was also on the receiving end of a bad tackle from Timothy Castagne in the second half that got the Fulham defender booked.

Manchester United confirmed both withdrawals on Mondy, along with backup goalkeeper Karl Darlow pulling out of the Wales squad. No specifics were given but each will be ‘assessed and undergo individual recovery plans’ over the next three weeks.

The Athletic writes that Manchester United have been managing Rashford’s hip since the 2026 World Cup, but it is now ruling him out of international duty. In a similar way to Cole Palmer’s withdrawal benefiting Chelsea because of a three-week rest, it could actually be a blessing in disguise for Rashford, who is yet to score or assist since rejoining the Red Devils.

Mainoo was pulled from the Fulham game after 80 minutes. The 21-year-old midfielder hasn’t played for England since World Cup warmups in June, having curiously been an unused substitute throughout the whole tournament.

Rashford will not add to his 78 England caps before November. /  Leonardo Fernandez/FIFA/Getty ImagesThree weeks out of the spotlight might help Rashford, who has been the center of attention since the decision was made during the summer that he would reintegrate after spending 18 months on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona.
The opportunity to rest, recover and work on his fitness when there has been a background problem that has clearly been bothering him is equally important.

United need Rashford more than ever following the international window. He remains the most recent player at the club to score 30 goals in a single season—and the only player to reach that milestone in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era, which came in 2022–23.

ftbpro_01m31vjzf7jq.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Tom Gott8:30 AM EDTAtlético Madrid held on to Julián Alvarez. / Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesAtlético Madrid had “no way to justify” their intentionally stubborn approach to the Julián Alvarez transfer saga this summer, Barcelona president Joan Laporta has claimed.

Reports of a bid worth €100 million ($116 million) surfaced towards the end of May and ignited a prickly feud between the two teams at Atlético did their best to resist Barcelona’s efforts to land the Argentine’s signature, even rebuffing Alvarez’s own public plea to leave the club.

Atlético repeatedly insisted they would not do business with Barcelona and looked too offload Alvarez elsewhere, with Arsenal known admirers, but the striker refused to deviate from his desire to move to Camp Nou. Ultimately, the biggest saga of the summer led to absolutely nothing.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

“They acted offended; they had no way to justify their attitude,” Laporta reflected. “We did what’s usually done: there was club-to-club communication, and then I spoke personally with [Atlético president] Gil Marín.
“He told me [Alvarez] wasn’t coming because they had no alternative. I told him that if they find one, he should tell us.

“Then they reacted inappropriately. I don’t know why, I have my suspicions, but I won’t say them publicly because I have no proof. We were constantly hearing that they would sell him to every club except Barça. Then they dropped the pretense and said it openly and acknowledged that we had called them.
“That is now in the past and we are very happy with the squad we have and the coach is very happy with the extraordinary work of Deco.”

Raphinha is flying this season. / Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto/Getty ImagesStriker was a priority area for Barcelona heading into the summer, with Robert Lewandowski leaving for the Chicago Fire and versatile backup Ferran Torres angling for a move away before joining Paris Saint-Germain. The focus had been on Alvarez long before the transfer window even opened.

Had Alvarez been granted his dream move to Barcelona, he would likely have been a success, albeit an incredibly expensive one. He’s a talented forward who knows how to score goals in Spain’s top flight.

With Atlético playing hardball, Barcelona had to get creative. Gabriel Jesus was recruited from Arsenal as affordable squad depth, but the real decision came with Raphinha beginning the campaign as the starting striker.

What initially seemed to be an effective stop-gap quickly exploded into the long-term solution. Barcelona’s attack has been the best on the planet this season and Raphinha, with 14 goals and three assists in eight games, has been right at the heart of that.
Would Alvarez have put up such numbers? It is impossible to know. Thankfully for Barcelona, they do not have to worry about hypotheticals because they have a striker making such a sensational impact.
Raphinha’s shift to striker has not only brought goal after goal, but it has also eased a selection headache facing manager Hansi Flick.

Lamine Yamal starts on the right wing, but who else makes up Barcelona’s front line behind the striker? Anthony Gordon was signed for big money on the left wing, where Raphinha spent most of his time last season. The Brazilian could have moved into attacking midfield, but Fermín López and Dani Olmo are already battling for minutes there. Flick seemed doomed to disappoint somebody, and there was reason to believe Raphinha would be the unhappy party.
Just a few weeks later, however, and Raphinha is on top of the world.

ftbpro_01m31wbejeet.title: ‘Really Poor’—Liverpool Legend’s Florian Wirtz Criticism Gives Headache to Andoni Iraola
ftbpro_01m31wbejeet.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Jamie Spencer9:00 AM EDTFlorian Wirtz is still not performing like Liverpool hoped. / David Horton/CameraSport/Getty ImagesJamie Carragher has challenged manager Andoni Iraola to make a tough decision on Florian Wirtz because, just over a year into his Liverpool career, the German No. 10, who was supposed to define the next Anfield chapter, might not be any more than a “neat and tidy” player worth half what the Reds paid last summer.

Wirtz was Liverpool’s first player signed for over £100 million ($133.9 million), a club-record buy until Alexander Isak also arrived a few weeks later. He was a Bundesliga champion at Bayer Leverkusen and a reliable source of goals and assists in the German scene—good but not outstanding numbers. Wirtz largely got the benefit of the doubt during his underwhelming debut season in England, but there are fewer and fewer places to hide with each passing match.

Carragher called Wirtz “really poor again” when Liverpool narrowly beat Bournemouth on Sunday. He started in the No. 10 role and was credited with three chances created, but his expected assists (xA) was just 0.05, while his expected goals (xG) was barely better at 0.22. Wirtz took no shots that weren’t blocked the moment the ball left his foot. His all-round game was only O.K. and he contributed very little where it actually mattered.

“Nothing is happening there at all,” Carragher sighed on Sky Sports.

“That was one of the poorest I’ve ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt. I’ve been critical of the fact that he hasn’t got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he’s neat and tidy, he keeps possession, there’s things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.”
But where the perception is now starting to change is Carragher no longer believes it is solely a matter of temporary form. Is this all that Florian Wirtz is?
“I worry [because] I don’t think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we’re seeing is what he is. It was just in the back of my head [for 12 months].

Wirtz does not threaten enough. /  Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images“I don’t see how he’s going to hurt you. It’s just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid. The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he’s given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.”

Carragher went on to suggest that the “gap” between the expectation and reality is “almost too big” for Wirtz to close. “You can’t get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it’s still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.”

Carragher namedropped Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall (Everton), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest) and Emiliano Buendía (Aston Villa) as attacking midfielders doing more for their respective clubs than Wirtz is at Liverpool. “No one out there would say Dewsbury-Hall is a better player than Wirtz … but every three or four weeks he scores a goal. These players aren’t going to get over £100 million, but they’re still giving their clubs bits every few weeks.”

Dominik Szoboszlai is best used further forward. / Steve Bardens/Getty ImagesCarragher doesn’t believe Iraola would be scared of making a big decision like benching Wirtz, especially with the Reds returning to Premier League action after the international window against Manchester City—it was a Wirtz performance against City in November of last season that prompted Gary Neville to brand him a “little boy” playing against men.
Iraola has seen fit to bench an underperforming Ryan Gravenberch for much of this season.

“Wirtz wouldn’t be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home, for me, he can't be in the team,” Carragher said. “The things I’ve liked so far about Iraola, he’s had the courage to make big decisions. Ryan Gravenberch has just signed a hefty contract on a five-year deal on massive money. He’s not playing. Sooner or later he's going to have to make a decision on Florian Wirtz. I hope it’s sooner. Not because I don’t like Florian Wirtz, I’m desperate for the kid to do well. I just want Liverpool to win.”

Wirtz moving to the bench would leave a perfect Dominik Szoboszlai-sized hole in the No. 10 berth. The Hungarian has generally been considered Liverpool’s best player since the start of last season, but has been accused in the early weeks of 2026–27 of lacking the positional discipline—through a natural keenness to be involved all over the pitch—of a traditional central midfielder.

If Szoboszlai gets into the No. 10 role at the expense of Wirtz, Liverpool get the best of him without the risk of leaving great holes in the middle of the pitch. If anything, Wirtz and Szoboszlai being in the same team means the latter has to play deeper and, as Carragher puts it, “I don’t think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player, I don’t.”

ftbpro_01m31ztw8qaf.title: Why Wrexham Have Bought The Turf Pub
ftbpro_01m31ztw8qaf.subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Rich Fay10:00 AM EDTThe Turf pub is a key part of the Wrexham football club and the Racecourse Ground. / Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty ImagesWrexham have completed the purchase of The Turf pub, which has been made famous by the Welcome to Wrexham docuseries.
The Welsh club announced Monday that it had exchanged contracts on the purchase of the iconic venue in a deal between the club’s parent company, Wrexham Holdings, and Admiral Taverns.

Wrexham’s decision to purchase The Turf is viewed as a key part of the club's future, while it will also allow them to preserve the history and tradition of the famous public house that is inexorably linked to the Racecourse Ground and the wider club.
It is believed that the club was founded at the previously named Turf Hotel in October 1864, making the Red Dragons the third-oldest professional team in the world.
FREE NEWSLETTER. New SI FC Newsletter Global Embed. Sign Up to Get Informed With SI FC. dark

A mural dedicated to Wrexham legend Joey Jones is on one side of The Turf. / Joe Prior/Getty ImagesWrexham insist the purchase of The Turf will not affect the daily running of the pub, with popular landlord Wayne Jones continuing in his role as usual.

As well as being extremely busy on matchdays, when it has become a key tourist attraction, the pub also forms a key part of the local community beyond soccer. It has been visited by several stars, including Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds, as well as fellow Hollywood stars Paul Rudd, Channing Tatum and Will Ferrell. Prince William also visited the pub to mark St. David’s Day in 2024.

In a statement released after the deal was announced, Turf landlord Jones assured supporters: “As landlord of The Turf for the past 20 years and a die-hard Wrexham fan, securing the pub’s future under Wrexham Holdings is great news for all Wrexham fans.

“The Turf Tavern, as it was then, predates the Club and records suggest that the Club itself was founded in the pub. It has played a key part of the Club’s history ever since, with the players changing in the pub before running out onto the Racecourse Ground as recently as the 1940s, and it continues to be a focal point for fans on matchdays and non-matchdays.
“I look forward to continuing to run The Turf and bringing its unique mix of history, atmosphere and sometimes Hollywood stardust to the next generation of Wrexham fans and locals alike.”

Those thoughts were echoed by Wrexham minority investor Eric Allyn, who added: “Ever since we invested in Wrexham AFC, the town, the community and the football club have become a second home. And no place more so than The Turf with Wayne Jones behind the bar and filled with the locals and international fans that visit regularly—they have all become our friends and have welcomed us into the Wrexham family.
“By bringing The Turf into the group, we are securing the long-term future of the pub and, with it, preserving its history and that of the Club.”

Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac have both signed the wall inside The Turf. / Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty ImagesWrexham claim the acquisition of The Turf will help protect the historic pub by incorporating it alongside the club and Racecourse Ground under a single ownership and “ring-fencing” it to protect the future of the club.

They also say it will allow for further investment in the fan experience in and around matchdays and provide an opportunity to enhance the current fan zone and other fan-related activities in the area next to the pub.
A planning application has already been approved to replace The Turf’s popular catering trailer with a new, modern shipping container, which will improve its ability to serve customers on matchdays.
Ultimately, the acquisition gives Wrexham total control over the business, which will make things much easier when it comes to any future stadium redevelopment project.

vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.title: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC: Dreyer strikes late to deny Messi and co.
vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.subtitle: Inter Miami's recent struggles continued as they played out yet another draw in MLS, losing more ground on the Eastern Conference leaders.
paragraphs: Anders Dreyer netted a late equaliser to earn San Diego FC a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami, who were held to a fourth straight stalemate despite Lionel Messi's free-kick.

Dreyer opened the scoring early on, but Miami turned the game on its head, with Messi and Luis Suarez both hitting the back of the net, only for San Diego's striker to complete his brace with eight minutes remaining at Nu Stadium.

San Diego's 12th-minute opener came out of nowhere as Jeppe Tverskov slotted a perfectly weighted throughball in behind for Dreyer, who charged in behind Miami's defense from the halfway line before dinking a lovely shot over Dayne St. Clair.
Twelve minutes later, Miami were back on level terms. Messi's free-kick looked to be more of a cross as it floated towards the far post, but it missed everyone in the middle and snuck in.

German Berterame's curler was cleared in front of the line by the retreating Ian Murphy, but San Diego could not clear their lines as Yannick Bright picked out Messi, whose first-time shot was kept out by CJ dos Santos.
Marcus Ingvartsen had a goal disallowed shortly after at the other end for an offside in the build-up, while Dos Santos punched away an awkward strike from Suarez.
But the Uruguayan soon got his goal in the 74th minute, lifting over Dos Santos from a tight angle to find the far corner.
Miami's lead only lasted eight minutes, though, with Dreyer again timing his run to perfection to meet a Tverskov pass, and a rooted St. Clair could not get a hand to it.

Messi had the chance to win it in stoppage time, bending a low shot through the crowded box, but Dos Santos got down to keep it out despite seeing it late, meaning Miami sit 11 points behind Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.
Messi makes more history despite Miami's frustrations
While Miami are unbeaten in their last five matches, they have drawn each of the last four, having held the lead in three of those.

But Messi has played his part in trying to get Miami back to winning ways, and netted his 101st goal for the Herons in total, while extending his lead in the Golden Boot race, as it was his 20th in MLS this season.
That means he is now just the second player in the league's history to score 20+ goals in three straight seasons, after Los Angeles FC's Denis Bouanga (2023-2025).
Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).
But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.
It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.title: Wirtz 'the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt' against Bournemouth, claims Carragher
vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.subtitle: Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact against Bournemouth, and Jamie Carragher has questioned his starting place going forward.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after the international break, claiming his performance against Bournemouth was the "poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt".
Liverpool edged to a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, giving Andoni Iraola a winning return to Vitality Stadium thanks to Alexander Isak's second-half goal.
Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983.
However, Wirtz came under fire for his performance on the south coast as he struggled to make an impact.
He finished the match with a team-low 70.3% passing accuracy (completing 26 of 37 passes), had 53 touches, and just two off-target shots, though he did create a joint-game-high three chances.
Only Ronald Araujo (24) lost possession more often than the German (16).
And Carragher was far from impressed by Wirtz's showing, claiming that Iraola needs to think about leaving him out of the side if they want to improve their results.
"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy; he keeps possession. There's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.
"But the reason I worry is: I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.
"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley, and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game, it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you.
"It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No. 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player; I don't.
"I think going forward, Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.
"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home; for me, he can't be in the team."
Wirtz has been called up in Jurgen Klopp's Germany squad for the upcoming Nations League.
Klopp – the former Liverpool manager – has named two squads, with Wirtz getting a rest before being in contention for their final two games of the international break against Serbia and Greece.
"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," Carragher added.

"Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he's obviously one of the best players in Germany; that's how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

"Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world; we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

"There's a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City's the next game; he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There's a potential turnaround there.
"I would love that to happen. I'd love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City."
Liverpool, who sit sixth in the Premier League table on nine points after an unbeaten start, return to action on October 11 against leaders Manchester City.
